citations.narrative:
Cleaning and sanitizing agents in labeled containers were observed loosely stored in a milk crate on the floor in the
animal food preparation area. Bulk storage of sanitizing agent (chlorine) was observed in boxes on a wooden pallet in a
garage / workshop area directly adjacent to the animal holding area.
Chemical contamination of animal food prior to, during, or after the food preparation process can lead to direct harm of the
animals consuming toxic substances. Cleaning and sanitizing agents, pesticides, and other potentially toxic agents must
be stored in secured cabinets designed and located to prevent contamination of food storage preparation surfaces.
Correct prior to the next relicense inspection.

Multiple non-exhibit and storage areas of the facility contain heavy accumulations of debris. Stacks and piles of
cardboard, boxes of mixed items, tools, holiday decorations, scrap wood, plastic, trash barrels, containers of various
chemicals, and scrap PVC pipe were piled against walls, on floors, and under and behind cabinets and shelves. Buildings
and grounds, as well as exhibit areas, must be kept clean and in good repair. Accumulated debris creates harborages,
nesting sites, and breeding grounds for insects, rodents, and other vermin that can harbor and transmit diseases or
contaminate the environment. Additionally, unmanaged materials—particularly loose chemical containers—pose direct
toxicological and physical safety hazards to the health and well-being of the animals while obstructing routine husbandry
and effective pest control interventions. Correct by removing all accumulated debris, trash, scrap materials, and unused
items from non-exhibit spaces; securely storing necessary chemicals and tools in designated cabinets; and implementing
a consistent housekeeping schedule to maintain clean premises. Correct before next relicense inspection.
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class C license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within (2 / 1) more inspection(s) or by (date-60 days counted from 1st RL Inspection) or
the applicant will forfeit the license fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your
next Re-License Inspection.
You may appeal this finding in writing by (insert date which is 7 days after issuance of report).
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
Additional Inspectors:
MacDonald Farnham, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
